fichas.title: Keeping Horses
fichas.summary: Guidance on horse welfare, social contact, group and individual housing, stable layout, and horse-related dimensions. Dimensions are generally based on withers height (Wh). The page gives sample withers heights for very large horses, average large horses, and ponies, plus formulas and example dimensions for boxes, passages, feeding stalls, and group stables. It recommends separating stallions and mares and providing group-kept horses with constant paddock access where shown.

The correct care according to the needs of the species is a precondition for the health, performance and tong life of the horse,
and also for its willingness and mental stability. Today, after 5000
years of domestication, the needs of horses are still similar to
those of wild animals on the steppes. Horses are herd animals
and social contact is essential. Whether kept in groups or singly,
attention should be paid to the social relationships and compatibility of horses. When horses are kept separately, ensure at least
sight, sound and smell contact between the animals. Foals and
young horses must grow up in groups.
Keeping in groups: This can be in single boxes or group boxes
with adjacent paddock.
Single boxes: Tie stalls are not to be recommended in the long
term. When horses are kept singly, a movement area at least as
large as a single box is better than none at all. Stables for heavy
horses should be planned with a ceiling height of at least 1.5 x
withers height, i.e. approx. ~2.70 m.

The correct care according to the needs of the species is a precondition for the health, performance and tong life of the horse,
and also for its willingness and mental stability. Today, after 5000
years of domestication, the needs of horses are still similar to
those of wild animals on the steppes. Horses are herd animals
and social contact is essential. Whether kept in groups or singly,
attention should be paid to the social relationships and compatibility of horses. When horses are kept separately, ensure at least
sight, sound and smell contact between the animals. Foals and
young horses must grow up in groups.
Keeping in groups: This can be in single boxes or group boxes
with adjacent paddock.
Single boxes: Tie stalls are not to be recommended in the long
term. When horses are kept singly, a movement area at least as
large as a single box is better than none at all. Stables for heavy
horses should be planned with a ceiling height of at least 1.5 x
withers height, i.e. approx. ~2.70 m.
